title: Checkpoint: Describe a variant
prompt: Implement `std::string describe(const std::variant<int, double, std::string>& v)` returning exactly `"int: 42"`, `"double: 3.50"` (always two decimals), or `"string: hi"` depending on the held alternative. Use `std::visit` with a generic lambda and `if constexpr` — no manual `index()` branching.

tests.name: int-case
tests.hint: The int branch prints the raw value.

tests.name: double-case
tests.code:
CHECK_EQ(describe(std::variant<int, double, std::string>{3.5}), std::string("double: 3.50"));
CHECK_EQ(describe(std::variant<int, double, std::string>{2.0}), std::string("double: 2.00"));
tests.hint: Two decimals, always — std::fixed with precision 2.

tests.name: string-case
tests.hint: The string branch passes the text through.
